stemBlocks.value: O is the origin, E lies on OF with OE = 2EF, and M is the midpoint of EG. Given OG = c and OF = d, find in terms of c and d, in simplest form: (i) FG, (ii) EG, (iii) OM.
Think first: OE = 2EF splits OF into three equal parts, so E is two-thirds of the way from O to F — write OE = (2/3)d before anything else.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p281-q04 from workbook page 281.

solutionSteps.instruction: Use OE = 2EF to split OF into three equal parts.
Find FG by subtracting the position vectors of F and G.
Find EG the same way, using the position vector of E.
Reach M by adding half of EG to OE, since M is the midpoint of EG.

strategyBlocks.value: Convert OE = 2EF into OE = (2/3)OF, then get FG and EG by subtracting position vectors, and reach M by going O → E → halfway along EG.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) FG = c − d  (ii) EG = c − (2/3)d  (iii) OM = (1/2)c + (1/3)d

whyThisWorks.value: The condition OE = 2EF says OE is twice EF, so OF is cut into three equal pieces and E sits at the two-thirds mark; that turns a worded ratio into the vector (2/3)d. From there every vector between two points is 'position of finish minus position of start'. A midpoint is exactly halfway, so adding half of EG to the position vector of E lands precisely on M.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading OE = 2EF as OE = 2OF and writing OE = 2d.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Reading OE = 2EF as OE = 2OF and writing OE = 2d.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing FG = d − c by reversing start and finish.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing FG = d − c by reversing start and finish.

commonErrors.misconception: Using OM = (1/2)(OE + OG) but substituting OF for OE.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using OM = (1/2)(OE + OG) but substituting OF for OE.

commonErrors.misconception: Failing to collect the d terms: (2/3)d − (1/3)d is (1/3)d, not (1/3)d subtracted.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Failing to collect the d terms: (2/3)d − (1/3)d is (1/3)d, not (1/3)d subtracted.

examTip.value: The midpoint of PQ always has position vector (1/2)(OP + OQ) — check your route answer against that formula as a free verification.
